title: Log regularity under saturated toric chart refinements
statement:
Let $(\operatorname{Spec}A,N)$ be a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme with fine saturated monoid chart $P\to A$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $Q$ be a finitely generated saturated submonoid of $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ containing $P$; thus $P^{\mathrm{gp}}\to Q^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is an isomorphism. Put
$$C=A\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q],$$
where $\mathbf Z[T]$ is the ring of finite sums of symbols $z^t$ with $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$, and tensor products are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$, with the log structure associated to $Q\to C$, is a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme. This includes $C=0$, with empty spectrum.

source.place: Expose VI, 1.8, printed p. 70 (log smooth maps preserve log regularity), applied to the group-isomorphism toric chart changes of Expose VIII, 3.3.11, printed p. 108; saturated blowup charts in 3.3.8--3.3.9.

proof.text: Write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $g:P\hookrightarrow Q$ be the inclusion. Since $Q$ is a submonoid of the group $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$, it is integral; together with its assumed finite generation and saturation this makes it fs [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The homomorphism $Q^{\mathrm{gp}}\to P^{\mathrm{gp}}$ induced by the inclusion is inverse to $g^{\mathrm{gp}}$: every $q\in Q$ is a difference of two elements of $P$, and these differences already generate $P^{\mathrm{gp}}$. Hence $g^{\mathrm{gp}}$ is injective with zero, in particular torsion-free, cokernel.

source.place: VIII 3.3.11, group-isomorphism toric charts; fs monoid conventions of VI 1.1.

proof.text: Apply [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] to the locally Noetherian scheme $Y$ and its affine open subscheme $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ itself, whose ring of sections is $A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]: $A$ is Noetherian. Choose monoid generators $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ of $Q$, allowing $r=0$. Then $C$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the finitely many elements $1\otimes z^{q_i}$. Indeed a tensor is a sum of pure tensors [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], each second factor is a finite integral linear combination of monomials $z^q$, and each $q$ is a sum of the $q_i$. The multiplication $(a\otimes u)(b\otimes v)=ab\otimes uv$ therefore expresses each pure tensor as an $A$-linear combination of products of these generators. Evaluation gives a surjection $A[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\twoheadrightarrow C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. The one-member affine open covering of $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$ by itself, with ring of sections $C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], shows that $X$ is locally Noetherian by the definition [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; properties.tex Tag 01OW, lemma-locally-Noetherian (affine open of a locally Noetherian scheme), Definition 01OV for the converse. Finite generators of the monoid algebra are written out.

proof.text: Let $\beta:Q\to C$ send $q$ to $1\otimes z^q$. Apply [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] to construct its associated log structure $M_X$. Its chart is $Q$, so $(X,M_X)$ is fs by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. The map $A\to C$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, defines $f:X\to Y$. The charts define a log morphism over $f$: a chart generator $p$ maps to the class of $g(p)$ and a local unit $u$ maps to $f^\sharp(u)$. In the chart pushout, the relation identifying $(p+e,u)$ with $(p,\alpha(e)u)$ maps to the same relation for $Q$, because $f^\sharp(\alpha(e))=\beta(g(e))$. These formulas agree under restriction and on overlaps, hence define the map of log sheaves $f^{-1}N\to M_X$. They also show compatibility with the structure maps. The chart description and universal property in [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks] identify the resulting source log structure with the one in the statement.

source.place: VI 1.1, associated log structures and charts; VIII 3.3.8–3.3.11, toric chart construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] with base ring $\mathbf Z[P]$ and algebras $A$ and $\mathbf Z[Q]$. It identifies $Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$, with both projections induced respectively by $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ and $z^q\mapsto1\otimes z^q$. Thus the comparison morphism for the charts of Step 3 is the identity of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ under this identification. It is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]: identity ring maps are finitely presented, flat, and have identity diagonal, an open immersion. This checks the comparison hypothesis, rather than asserting that the underlying morphism $f$ itself is etale.

source.place: Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes) and 01JQ (lemma-fibre-product-affines); morphisms.tex Tag 02GI for the etale identity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] to $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,N)$. Both log schemes are locally Noetherian and fs by Steps 1–3; the target is log regular by hypothesis. The compatible global charts $P\to N$, $Q\to M_X$ have injective group map with torsion-free cokernel by Step 1, and their comparison is etale by Step 4. All hypotheses of that node are therefore satisfied. Its log-regular-source conclusion proves that $(\operatorname{Spec}C,M_X)$ is log regular, which is the remaining assertion.

source.place: VI 1.8, log smooth morphisms over a log regular base have log regular source; VIII 3.3.11, toric log-etale chart changes.

proof.text: If $C=0$, $X$ is empty: the zero ring has no prime ideals. The constructions above still apply, and the conditions of log regularity at geometric points in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] are vacuous. Thus no nonemptiness, injectivity of $A\to C$, or nonzero-ring condition was used.

source.place: VI 1.2, log regularity is a condition at points; empty chart convention.

proof_origin.place: VI 1.8 and VIII 3.3.11; affine Noetherian and fibre-product bookkeeping from Stacks 00FN, 01OW, 01I4, 01JQ.

lean.statement: theorem logRegular_toricChartRefinement (Y : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (eA : Y.scheme ≅ Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of A))) (hY : Y.IsLogRegular) (P : Type u) [CommMonoid P] (pFine : IsFineSaturatedMonoid P) (β : P →* A) (βY : P →* Y.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.scheme)))) (hβY : Y.logStructure.IsChart (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.scheme)) βY) (hβ : ∀ p : P, Y.logStructure.alpha.app (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.scheme))) (βY p) = eA.hom.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv (β p))) (Q : Submonoid (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P)) (qFine : IsFineSaturatedMonoid Q) (i : P →* Q) (hi : ∀ p : P, (i p : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P) = Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of p) : ∃ (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (eC : X.scheme ≅ Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of (toricChartRing β Q i)))) (βX : Q →* X.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X.scheme)))), X.IsLogRegular ∧ X.logStructure.IsChart (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X.scheme)) βX ∧ ∀ q : Q, X.logStructure.alpha.app (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X.scheme))) (βX q) = eC.hom.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of (toricChartRing β Q i))).inv (toricChartMap β Q i q))
lean.note: The explicit tensor ring and canonical chart are real constructions. Global IsChart plus structural compatibility characterizes the associated log structure; no change to the natural-language statement is needed.
